workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(filesystem): report a missing parent directory, not a raw chdir error. Target files: src/filesystem/pinned-directory.ts, src/filesystem/__tests__/append-file.test.ts, src/filesystem/__tests__/missing-parent-error.test.ts. A pinned write whose parent directory is missing failed with Node's raw `chdir` error, which named `chdir` (an implementation detail of the pinned-directory anchor) and the **server process's working directory** (wherever the client launched it, possibly outside the allowed directories). `e... (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5448)

workarounds.symptom: filesystem: edit_file's whitespace-tolerant match fails when oldText ends with a newline
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(filesystem): match edit_file oldText that ends with a newline. Target files: src/filesystem/lib.ts, src/filesystem/__tests__/edit-trailing-newline.test.ts, .changeset/filesystem-5431-edit-trailing-newline.md. `edit_file`'s whitespace-tolerant fallback split `oldText` on `\n`, so a trailing newline became an empty last "line" that had to equal the file's next line. Whole lines copied with their final newline therefore failed to match whenever only indentation differed. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/pull/5447)

workarounds.symptom: mcp-server-fetch: `fetch` prompt returns JSON-RPC error code 0 with the raw exception text for an invalid URL
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(fetch): reject an invalid prompt URL with -32602. Target files: src/fetch/src/mcp_server_fetch/server.py, src/fetch/tests/test_prompt_url.py, src/fetch/tests/test_protocol.py. The `fetch` prompt passed its `url` argument straight to httpx. A malformed URL such as `http://[::1` raises `httpx.InvalidURL`, which is not an `httpx.HTTPError`, so it escaped `fetch_url`'s handler and the prompt's `except ToolError`, and the SDK answered with its generic fallback for an unhandled exception. workarounds.symptom: Client never retries after -32020 HeaderMismatch, and there is no public way to pre-load the x-mcp-header map (SEP-2243 client SHOULD/MAY both unimplemented)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Retry a tool call once after a HeaderMismatch rejection. Target files: src/mcp/client/client.py, tests/docs_src/test_header_parameters.py, tests/interaction/_requirements.py. On a 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP connection, `Client.call_tool` for a tool with `x-mcp-header` arguments failed with `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) unless that client had already listed the tool. It also kept failing when the tool's schema gained an annotation after it was listed. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3627)

workarounds.symptom: test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape fails on Windows without elevation or Developer Mode
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fall back to an NTFS junction when the symlink escape test can't create a symlink. Target files: tests/shared/test_path_security.py. `test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape` called `symlink_to()` unguarded. Windows only allows that for elevated processes or with Developer Mode on, so on an ordinary Windows dev machine the test errored with `WinError 1314` before it ever reached `safe_join`. CI didn't notice because the hosted Windows runners are allowed to create symlinks. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3609)

workarounds.symptom: Client.listTools() silently drops pages when a server repeats a cursor
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(client): follow nextCursor until it is absent; stop on a repeated page. A bare `listTools()` / `listPrompts()` / `listResources()` / `listResourceTemplates()` call stopped its page walk as soon as the server sent a `nextCursor` it had sent before, and returned the short list silently with no `nextCursor`.
